issues.legal_issue: A retrospective validating law is constitutionally valid when the legislature has competence over the subject, removes the legal basis of the earlier judgment, and complies with constitutional limitations.
material_facts: The earlier judgment held that the building permission conflicted with a zoning restriction limiting new buildings to 55 feet.
The legislature retrospectively raised the permitted building height to above 165 feet and provided for regularisation of certain deviations.
The challenged law applied the changed zoning rule retrospectively to the period during which the earlier restriction had been in force.
issues.conclusion: The law was constitutionally valid because it materially changed the zoning rule on which the earlier judgment rested and thereby removed the basis of that judgment before validating the relevant construction.
issues.legal_principle: A legislature with competence over the subject may enact retrospective legislation and validate past acts if it removes the defect or legal basis that led to the earlier decision; it cannot merely declare that the decision is not binding. The law must also comply with constitutional limitations, including Part III. The Court applied Shri Prithvi Cotton Mills v. Broach Borough Municipality (1970) 2 SCC 388; Government of Andhra Pradesh v. Hindustan Machine Tools Ltd. (1975 Supp SCR 394); Hindustan Gum and Chemicals Ltd. v. State of Haryana (1985) 4 SCC 124; Vijay Mills Company Ltd. v. State of Gujarat (1993) 1 SCC 345; and Indian Aluminium Co. v. State of Kerala (1996) 7 SCC 637, among other decisions.

rule.if: challenge_to_retrospective_validating_law and legislature_has_subject_matter_competence and earlier_decision_rest_on_prior_legal_restriction and legislature_retroactively_removed_that_restriction and law_complies_with_constitutional_limits

predicates.challenge_to_retrospective_validating_la: A party challenged a law that retrospectively validates earlier acts.
predicates.legislature_has_subject_matter_competenc: The legislature had authority to make laws on the subject addressed by the challenged law.
predicates.earlier_decision_rest_on_prior_legal_res: An earlier court decision relied on a legal restriction that governed the conduct in dispute.
predicates.legislature_retroactively_removed_that_r: The legislature changed that restriction retrospectively so that the earlier decision would not follow under the changed law.
predicates.law_complies_with_constitutional_limits: The challenged law does not violate applicable constitutional limitations.
predicates.validating_law_is_constitutionally_valid: The retrospective validating law is constitutionally valid.

issues.definition: When a challenge to a retrospective validating law concerns conduct governed by a restriction that the legislature competently and constitutionally changed with retrospective effect, the law is valid if that change removes the basis of the earlier decision.

issues.legal_issue: A legislature's alleged purpose of defeating an earlier judicial decision does not by itself invalidate a law that changes the governing legal rule.
material_facts: The respondents argued that the law was intended to nullify the earlier judgment and relied on its Statement of Objects and Reasons.
The law retrospectively changed the applicable building-height rule rather than merely declaring the earlier judgment non-binding.
issues.conclusion: The alleged legislative intention to defeat the earlier judgment did not invalidate the law; legislative motive was not open to judicial scrutiny as a ground of invalidity.
issues.legal_principle: The validity of legislation is determined by its constitutionality, not by an asserted legislative motive. A Statement of Objects and Reasons may be referred to for limited purposes, such as understanding factual background and the circumstances addressed, but cannot alone be the basis for invalidating a statute. The Court relied on T. Venkata Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1985) 3 SCC 198 and Gurudevdatta VKSS Maryadit v. State of Maharashtra (2001) 4 SCC 534.

predicates.challenge_to_legislation: A party challenged the constitutionality of a legislative enactment.
predicates.alleged_legislative_motive_is_to_defeat_: The challenger asserted that the legislature enacted the law to defeat an earlier judicial decision.
predicates.law_changes_the_governing_legal_rule: The enactment changes the legal rule governing the conduct addressed by the earlier decision.
predicates.alleged_motive_alone_does_not_invalidate: The asserted purpose of defeating an earlier judgment, by itself, does not make the law invalid.

issues.definition: When legislation is challenged and the asserted purpose is to defeat an earlier judgment, that motive alone does not invalidate the law if the enactment changes the governing legal rule.

issues.legal_issue: A legislature may establish a zoning rule directly in a retrospective enactment without amending the parent planning statute or using that statute's procedure for making zoning regulations.
material_facts: The challenged enactment placed the revised maximum building height in its own schedule and gave the revision retrospective effect.
The respondents argued that the parent planning statute and its procedure for framing zoning regulations had not been amended or followed.
The enactment replaced the earlier height restriction for the period when the outline plan had operated.
issues.conclusion: The legislature was not required to amend the parent planning statute or follow its procedure for framing zoning regulations because the enactment itself established the revised rule retrospectively.
issues.legal_principle: A competent legislature may make a retrospective change to the governing law, and the consequences of such a change are assessed on the premise that the amended law was in force throughout the retrospective period. The legislature may place the revised rule directly in the enactment, rather than amend the parent statute's procedure for delegated regulation-making.

predicates.challenge_to_retrospective_zoning_law: A party challenged a law that retrospectively changes a zoning rule.
predicates.legislature_places_revised_rule_in_enact: The legislature states the revised zoning rule directly in the enactment.
predicates.revised_rule_applies_retroactively: The revised rule is made applicable to a period before the enactment took effect.
predicates.parent_statute_provides_a_regulation_mak: The existing parent statute provides a procedure for an authority to make zoning regulations.
predicates.separate_amendment_of_parent_statute_is_: The legislature need not separately amend the parent statute's regulation-making procedure to establish the retrospective rule.

issues.definition: When a challenged retrospective zoning law states the revised rule directly and applies it to an earlier period, the parent statute's separate regulation-making procedure need not itself be amended.
